prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-11-06. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.32 |
| Retained earnings       | 68,459M |
| Current liabilities     | 12,009M |
| Current assets          | 15,884M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 64,923M |
| Total liabilities       | 57,549M |
| Total assets            | 122,472M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,702M |
| Revenue                 | 14,969M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-11-06, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided data show a very large, mature company with moderate leverage (total liabilities ~47% of assets), ample equity coverage, strong cumulative profitability (retained earnings exceed equity), an acceptable liquidity buffer (current ratio 1.32), and solid operating margins (~18%). These metrics collectively support an upper-medium-grade profile, though the absence of interest-coverage or cash-flow data and the merely adequate current ratio prevent an AA categorization.
DECISION: A-
(The data are also consistent with an A or A+ rating, but A- is the single most defensible label given the information constraints.)
